title: Perfect Privacy of Threshold Sharing
statement: Let $F$ be a field, let $k$ be a natural number, and consider the scheme that shares a secret $s\in F$ by evaluating $s+Xq(X)$ at nonzero field elements, where $q$ has degree less than $k-1$; reconstruction from a set of parties evaluates the interpolating polynomial at zero. For every finite set $B$ of nonzero field elements with $|B|<k$ and every pair of secrets $s,s'\in F$, there is a bijection $e$ of the randomness space such that, for every randomness choice $r$ and every $b\in B$, the share of $s'$ using randomness $e(r)$ at $b$ equals the share of $s$ using randomness $r$ at $b$.
hypotheses_covered: $B$ is a finite set of nonzero field elements
$B$ is unauthorized for the threshold-$k$ access structure, equivalently $|B|<k$
